proposition_text: For the purposes of records of spreading nitrogen fertiliser, the area of the holding excludes any land on which the occupier does not spread fertiliser or work the soil.
The maximum amount of poultry manure that may be spread at any one time is 8 tonnes per hectare.
The occupier of a holding must not store organic manure (other than slurry), or bedding contaminated with organic manure, except on an impermeable surface.
Records of spreading nitrogen fertiliser must include the quantity of organic manure spread.

Where samples are collected to calculate compliance with the whole farm limit for pigs and poultry, four samples for analysis must be taken in a calendar year — one in each quarter — from manure heaps not more than 12 months old.
Organic manure must be incorporated into the ground using equipment of a kind described in regulation 17(4)(a) or (c).
The implementation report must be published in such manner as the Secretary of State considers appropriate.
An application relating to the calendar year commencing on 1st January 2017 may be submitted by 20th March 2017.
A person planning the spreading of nitrogen fertiliser must produce a fertilisation plan for that growing season.
A derogation from the nitrate action programme requirements is subject to the conditions set out in Schedule 3, as provided under Regulation 36(4).
There must be at least three weeks between any spreading of organic manure of the descriptions specified in paragraph (a) or (b) of regulation 20.
A person having custody or control of slurry must store it only in a slurry storage system that satisfies the requirements of Schedule 2.
The occupier of a holding who has used nitrogen fertiliser must record the yield achieved by an arable crop within one week of ascertaining it.

Where there is more than one fuel storage tank within the storage area and fuel oil is not otherwise stored there, the surrounding bund must be capable of retaining a volume of fuel oil not less than the greater of: (i) 110 per cent of the capacity of the largest tank within the area, or (ii) 25 per cent of the total volume of oil that could be stored in all tanks within the area.
The fertilisation plan must record the soil type in relation to the area planted or intended to be planted.
Silage must be kept in a silo that satisfies the requirements of Schedule 1.
The occupier must calculate the amount of phosphorus in the soil that is likely to be available for uptake by the crop during the growing season.
In the case of brassica, an additional 50 kg of nitrogen per hectare may be spread every four weeks during the closed period up to the date of harvest.
The competent authority must notify the applicant in writing of its determination of a derogation application.

The occupier of a holding must not store organic manure (other than slurry), or bedding contaminated with organic manure, except, in the case of solid manure which can be stacked in a free-standing heap and which does not drain liquid from the material, on a temporary field site.

The permitted amount of nitrogen (kg/ha) and standard yield (tonne/ha) for each crop listed in the table are the values referred to in regulation 12(1) for the purposes of determining total nitrogen spread on a holding.
A slurry storage tank with walls made of earth must not be filled to a level that allows less than 750 millimetres of freeboard.
A record required under paragraph 15 must be made by 1st March for the calendar year concerned.
The occupier must keep a record of the application and determination.
The implementation report must be submitted by the last day of the six-month period beginning with the day on which the relevant period ends.

The occupier of a new holding with livestock must calculate and record the amount of manure that will be produced by the number of animals expected to be kept in a building or on hardstanding during the storage period, using the figures in Schedule 1.

In the case of permanently housed pigs or poultry, the occupier may use software approved by the Secretary of State as an alternative method for calculating nitrogen produced by animals on the holding.

A person may spread organic manure with high readily available nitrogen on tillage land with sandy or shallow soil during the period beginning 1st August and ending the following 15th September, notwithstanding the closed period in paragraph (2)(b), provided the next crop sown on the land is sown on or before 15th September.
If necessary, the Secretary of State must revise or add to the designation of nitrate vulnerable zones.
Where a system of keeping livestock only produces solid manure, the nitrogen produced by animals on the holding must be determined by sampling and analysis in accordance with Part 2 of Schedule 2.
When planning the spreading of nitrogen fertiliser, the plan must include the area of the field planted or intended to be planted.

In assessing the risk of nitrogen getting into surface water, account must be taken in particular of: (a) the slope of the land (especially if greater than 12 degrees); (b) any ground cover; (c) the proximity to surface water; (d) the weather conditions; (e) the soil type; and (f) the presence of land drains.
Regulation 20 (closed periods for organic manure) does not apply to the spreading of nitrogen fertiliser in a greenhouse.
Fuel oil on farms must be stored in a fuel storage tank within a storage area or facility that satisfies the requirements of Schedule 3.
The storage provisions do not apply to the temporary storage of fuel oil in a tanker used for transporting fuel oil on roads or about a farm.
The occupier must not bring organic manure on to the holding.

Where a silo has a capacity of 1,500 cubic metres or more, the capacity of the effluent tank must not be less than 30 cubic metres plus 6.7 litres for each cubic metre of silo capacity in excess of 1,500 cubic metres.

When planning the spreading of nitrogen fertiliser, a person must calculate the amount of nitrogen in the soil that is likely to be available for uptake by the crop concerned during the growing season.
The authority may withdraw a notice issued under regulation 7.

The prohibition in regulation 17(2) does not apply where organic manure is spread on land managed for breeding wader birds or as a species-rich semi-natural grassland and the land comes within paragraph (3).
Livestock manure (other than slurry or poultry manure) may be spread only in the period beginning 1st June and ending the following 31st October.

On an organic holding, nitrogen fertiliser may be spread on any crop other than a grass crop in accordance with written advice from a FACTS adviser, as an exemption from the general spreading controls.

The occupier of a new holding with livestock must calculate and record the amount of storage capacity (in slurry vessels and hardstanding) required to enable compliance with regulation 25, taking into account the amount of manure intended to be exported from the holding, the amount intended to be spread on land with a low run-off risk, and, in the case of a slurry vessel, the amount of liquids other than slurry likely to enter the vessel.

A report under regulation 40A(1) must contain: (a) details of any steps taken to promote good agricultural practice; (b) the map published under regulation 3(2) accompanied by a statement detailing the nature of and reasons for any revisions to the designated nitrate vulnerable zone since the end of the previous reporting period; (c) a summary of the monitoring results obtained by the Agency under regulation 4; and (d) a summary of the most recent review conducted under regulation 39.
In the case of winter oilseed rape on an organic holding, nitrogen must not be spread after 31st October.
An occupier of a holding who keeps any animals specified in column 1 of Schedule 1 must provide sufficient storage for all slurry produced on the holding during the storage period.
For the purposes of paragraph (5), the total amount of nitrogen in organic manure is to be calculated by reference to the methods described in regulation 14.
The review of the action programme must include the decisions taken and the reasons for them.
Records of spreading nitrogen fertiliser must include the method of spreading.

The slurry storage tank and any effluent tank, channels, pipes and reception pit must be designed and constructed so that, with proper maintenance, they are likely to continue to satisfy the requirements of paragraphs 2 to 4 for at least 20 years.

No later than the end of each four-year period, the Secretary of State must identify land which drains into waters identified under subparagraph (a), or into water similarly identified in Wales or Scotland, and that contributes to the pollution in those waters.
A person must not spread organic manure within 50 metres of a borehole, spring or well.

A person who has custody or control of a silage bale must not open or remove the wrapping of the bale within 10 metres of any inland freshwaters or coastal waters which silage effluent could enter as a result.

Before spreading organic manure, the occupier must record the amount of phosphate likely to be supplied from the organic manure intended to be spread for the purpose of fertilising the crop in the growing season in which it is spread.
Organic manure must not be spread if it is spread in the period beginning 1st June and ending the following 31st October.
The base of the silo, the base and walls of its effluent tank and channels, and the walls of any pipes must be impermeable.
A notice issued under regulation 7 must inform the person of the effect of regulation 8.

The accounts must record the total agricultural area of the holding, the area covered by each specified crop type (winter wheat, spring wheat, winter barley, spring barley, winter oilseed rape, sugar beet, potatoes, forage maize, grass, and other crops), and the number and category of animals kept on the holding by reference to Schedule 1.

When planning the spreading of nitrogen fertiliser, a farmer must take into account the optimum amount of nitrogen that should be spread on the crop, having regard to the amount of nitrogen calculated under paragraph (1)(a).

Regulation 25 does not apply to a new holding until the latest date on which a closed period under regulation 20 begins in relation to that holding, regardless of whether an exception under regulation 20(4) or 21 applies.
The occupier must not bring organic manure on to the holding.
When planning the spreading of nitrogen fertiliser, the type of crop must be taken into account.
A condition for the application of a higher nitrogen limit is that at least 80% of the holding's agricultural area is sown with grass.
For solid manures, at least ten samples of 1 kg each must be taken, each from a different location in a heap, and each sample must be taken at least 0.5 metres from the surface of the heap.
Before spreading organic manure, the occupier must record the total phosphate content of the organic manure.

Condition 2 requires that the total amount of nitrogen in the form of green compost or green/food compost spread on any given hectare of land on the holding does not exceed 500kg in any two-year period, whether spread as mulch or incorporated into the soil.

The dual valve requirement in sub-paragraph (1) does not apply where a slurry storage tank drains through the pipe into another slurry storage tank of equal or greater capacity, or where the tops of the tanks are at the same level.
A regulatory review must include an assessment of the extent to which the relevant objectives are being achieved.

A person who proposes to have custody or control of silage, slurry or fuel oil to be kept in a new or improved store must give the Agency notice specifying the type of silo or storage system and its location at least 14 days before work constructing the new or improved store is to be begun.
The Secretary of State must from time to time carry out a review of these Regulations, in so far as the Secretary of State has not done so under regulation 39.
In the case of permanent grassland, the occupier must comply with the duty to plan the spreading of nitrogen fertiliser each calendar year before the first spreading of nitrogen fertiliser.
The reference to 'agricultural area' in paragraph (1) does not include any land covered by a greenhouse.
The base and walls of a silo, its effluent tank and channels, and the walls of any pipes must, so far as reasonably practicable, be resistant to attack by silage effluent.

In the case of any crop other than those covered by regulation 10(1)'s primary timing rule, the occupier must comply with the duty under paragraph (1) before spreading any nitrogen fertiliser for the first time for the purpose of fertilising a crop planted or intended to be planted.

The Agency may serve a notice on a person who has custody or control of silage, slurry or fuel oil, or is responsible for the silo, slurry storage system or fuel oil storage tank, in circumstances in which these Regulations apply, requiring that person to carry out works, or take precautions or other steps, specified in the notice.

In the case of brassica, an additional 50 kg of nitrogen per hectare may be spread every four weeks during the applicable closed period under regulation 20, up to the date of harvest, but not so as to exceed the limit imposed by paragraph (2).
A risk map must show each field with its area in hectares.
A review must identify land which drains into nitrate-polluted waters, or into water similarly identified in Wales or Scotland, and that contributes to the pollution in those waters.
A slurry store must have the capacity to store, in addition to the manure, any rainfall, washings or other liquid that enters the vessel (either directly or indirectly) during the storage period.
A risk map must include all surface waters.
For the purposes of calculating the area of the holding under paragraph (7), land on which the occupier does not spread fertiliser or work the soil is excluded from that area.
The occupier must maintain the holding to ensure that at least 80% of the agricultural area is sown with grass during the calendar year to which the derogation applies.
The occupier must make a record of the type and amount of livestock manure intended to be sent off the holding during the calendar year to which the derogation relates.
Storage for organic manure must be sited at least 50 metres from a watercourse or conduit leading to a watercourse.

A person who has custody or control of field silage or silage stored on open land must ensure that the Agency is given notice of the place where the silage is to be made or stored at least 14 days before the place is first used for that purpose.
The amount of nitrogen available for crop uptake from organic manure may be calculated by reference to the values given in the Fertiliser Manual (as described in paragraph (4)(a) of that Manual).
The bund and the base of the area must be impermeable to water and oil.
A dribble bar applicator is a permitted method of spreading organic manure near surface water, boreholes, springs or wells under the conditions set out in regulation 17(4).
An occupier who sends livestock manure off a holding must, within one week of doing so, record the name and address of the recipient.
The total amount of nitrogen in organic manure applied to a holding, whether directly by an animal or by spreading, must not exceed 100 kg multiplied by the area of the holding in hectares.
Organic manure may be stored in a covered building (including a greenhouse).

A report under regulation 40(2)(a) must include an assessment of whether the objectives of these Regulations remain appropriate and, in so far as they do, the extent to which they could be achieved in a less burdensome way.
The base of a silo must be provided at its perimeter with channels designed and constructed so as to collect any silage effluent that escapes from the silo.
When planning the spreading of nitrogen fertiliser on arable land, the plan must include the expected yield.
For the purposes of regulation 36(2), paragraph 2(b) of Annex 3 to Council Directive 91/676/EEC is to be read as if the third subparagraph were omitted.
The base of a silo must be designed in accordance with BS 8007: 1987 (the British Standards Institution code of practice for design of concrete structures for retaining aqueous liquids).

Records must include the amount of storage capacity (in slurry vessels and hardstanding) required to enable compliance with regulation 25, taking into account the amount of manure intended to be exported from the holding.

The occupier may rely on the result of previous phosphorus soil sampling and analysis of the agricultural area of the derogated holding under the same cropping regime and soil type for the purposes of the four-yearly sampling obligation, provided the sampling and analysis was carried out within four years before the grant of the derogation.
Fuel oil on farms may be stored in an underground fuel storage tank.

Where there is only one fuel storage tank within the storage area and fuel oil is not otherwise stored there, the surrounding bund must be capable of retaining a volume of fuel oil not less than 110 per cent of the capacity of that tank.
A person must not spread manufactured nitrogen fertiliser within 2 metres of surface water.
Where fuel from a tank is delivered through a permanently attached flexible pipe, the pipe must be fitted with a tap or valve at its end that closes automatically when not in use.

In the case of tillage land with soil of a type specified in the first column of the table, the closed period for spreading organic manure is the period beginning with the first date specified in relation to that soil type in the third column of the table and ending with the second date so specified.
If necessary, the Secretary of State must revise the restrictions following a review of the action programme.

Where silage is a crop being made into field silage or silage being stored on open land, the Agency must be given notice of the place where the silage is to be made or stored at least 14 days before the place is first used for that purpose.
The occupier must make a record describing the livestock housing and manure storage systems together with the volume of manure storage in place on the holding by 1st March for each calendar year.
The occupier must calculate the optimum amount of phosphate fertiliser that should be spread on the crop, taking into account the amount of available phosphorus calculated under paragraph (a).
Crop rotation on the holding must not include leguminous or other plants fixing atmospheric nitrogen, except where the leguminous plant is grass containing less than 50% clover.
A condition for the application of a higher nitrogen limit is that at least 80% of the holding's agricultural area is sown with grass.
When determining restrictions on spreading nitrogen fertiliser, the proximity to surface water must be taken into account.
An occupier of a holding who spreads organic manure on that holding must produce and maintain a risk map showing each field with its area in hectares.
Regulation 19 does not apply to nitrogen fertiliser spread in a greenhouse.

Where phosphorus soil sampling and analysis of the agricultural area of the derogated holding under the same cropping regime and soil type has not been carried out within four years before the grant of the derogation, such sampling and analysis must be carried out on 100% of the agricultural area no later than 12 months after the date on which a derogation is next granted to the occupier.
The reference in paragraph (1) to the land on the holding does not include any land which is covered by a greenhouse for the whole of the period concerned.
The Secretary of State must set out the conclusions of the regulatory review in a report.
The Agency must refuse a derogation application if the occupier has been found in breach of the derogation conditions during the calendar year preceding that to which the application relates.

A slurry storage tank must have adequate storage capacity for the likely quantities of slurry produced from time to time on the premises, taking into account the proposed method of utilising the slurry and the likely rates and times of utilisation, as well as the matters in sub-paragraph (3).

After acting in reliance on regulation 13, the occupier must provide the FACTS adviser with soil analyses from representative autumn soil samples so that the adviser may take the analyses into account when advising for the purposes of paragraph (2) in relation to subsequent years.
The risk map for the holding must correspond with the agricultural area of the holding.

Where silage is a crop being made into field silage or silage being stored on open land, the place must be at least 10 metres from any inland freshwaters or coastal waters, and at least 50 metres from the nearest relevant abstraction point of any protected water supply source that silage effluent could enter if it escaped.
The occupier must calculate the amount of nitrogen in the manure produced by the animals on the holding during that year by reference to Schedule 1.
In the case of winter oilseed rape, nitrogen must not be spread after 31st October.

An exemption applies in relation to a structure for which a contract for its construction, substantial enlargement or substantial reconstruction was entered into before 1st March 1991, and the work was completed before 1st September 1991.

Where a silo has retaining walls, the silo must at no time be loaded to a depth exceeding the maximum depth consistent with the design assumption made in respect of the loadings of the retaining walls.
For tillage land on sandy or shallow soil, the closed period for spreading organic manure runs from 1st August to the following 31st December.
A record must be kept of the number of animals on the holding during the previous calendar year and the category for each animal by reference to Schedule 1.
A person must not spread organic manure with high readily available nitrogen on land during the closed period.
No later than the end of each four-year period, the Secretary of State must, if necessary, revise or add to the designation of nitrate vulnerable zones.
Records of spreading nitrogen fertiliser must include the date of spreading.

Organic manure in the form of slurry, sewage sludge or anaerobic digestate (or any combination) may be spread using a trailing hose band spreader or a trailing shoe band spreader, except within 6 metres of surface water.

Each sample must be taken from a vessel; but if a tanker used for spreading is fitted with a suitable valve, the samples may be taken while spreading and each sample must be taken at intervals during the spreading.
Livestock manure must not be applied to surface waters, hardstanding, buildings, roads, or woodland (unless the woodland is used for grazing).
The occupier must record, within one week of spreading manufactured phosphate fertiliser, the date of spreading.
The regulatory review must set out the objectives intended to be achieved by these Regulations.

Any other organic manure (other than organic manure spread as a mulch on sandy soil) must be incorporated as soon as practicable (and within 24 hours at the latest), if the land— is within 50 metres of surface water, and
A person on whom a regulation 7 notice has been served must comply with the requirements of that notice.

The occupier of a holding must ensure that, in any calendar year, the total amount of nitrogen in livestock manure applied to the holding (whether directly by an animal or by spreading) does not exceed 170 kg multiplied by the area of the holding in hectares.
The implementation report must include a summary of the most recent review conducted under regulation 39.
A plan for the spreading of nitrogen fertiliser must record the amount calculated under paragraph (1)(a) and the method used to calculate that figure.
The Secretary of State must, by 1st March 2017, send written notice to any person appearing to the Secretary of State to be the owner or occupier of a relevant holding.
The objectives of the derogation application include reducing water pollution caused or induced by nitrates from agricultural sources.
An offence or penalty provision under regulation 41 applies to a person who was purporting to act in the capacity of an officer or similar role.
When planning the spreading of nitrogen fertiliser, the farmer must take into account the previous crop and, if that crop was grass, whether it was managed by cutting or grazing.
The period within which works etc. must be carried out pursuant to a notice under regulation 7 may be such longer period as is reasonable in the circumstances.
On an organic holding, nitrogen must not be spread after 31st October.
Where any grass on the holding is ploughed, the land must be sown with grass within six weeks beginning with the day after the ploughing.
A person must record the area on which the manure is to be spread.
These Regulations apply to England only.
A plan for the spreading of nitrogen fertiliser must include the reference or name of the relevant field.
Part 4 does not apply to the spreading of nitrogen fertiliser on a crop growing in a greenhouse.

Records must include the amount of manure that will be produced by the number of animals expected to be kept in a building or on hardstanding during the storage period, calculated using the figures given in Schedule 1.
The provisions of the Order relating to the civil sanctions referred to in paragraph (1) apply as if they were provisions of these Regulations.
For grassland on sandy or shallow soil, the closed period for spreading organic manure runs from 1st September to the following 31st December.

Objective criteria for derogation applications must include the existence, in designated nitrate vulnerable zones, of long growing seasons, crops with high nitrogen uptake, and soils with exceptionally high denitrification capacity.

The public must be given an opportunity to express comments and opinions on the review of the action programme when all options are under consideration and before decisions on the plans and programmes are made.

The following regulations do not apply in relation to a new holding until 31st July in the third calendar year after the year in which the Secretary of State revises or adds to the designation of nitrate vulnerable zones under regulation 4(5) so as to include the new holding— regulation 22 (closed period for manufactured nitrogen fertiliser)
If the Agency grants a derogation application, it must designate the holding in question as a derogated holding for the calendar year to which the application relates.

A notice under paragraph (3)(b) or (3A)(b) must contain a reference to the page on the Agency's or Secretary of State's website on which can be found the Secretary of State's proposals or, in the case of a notice under paragraph (3A)(b) where the designation has already been revised or added to, the designation.
For the purposes of regulation 13, the total amount of nitrogen from organic manure must be calculated by reference to the methods described in regulation 14 for establishing available nitrogen.
A maximum of 40 kg of nitrogen per hectare may be spread at any one time on an organic holding.
A person must not spread organic manure within 10 metres of surface water.

At least every four years, the occupier of a derogated holding must undertake soil sampling and analysis for the supply of phosphorus of at least every five hectares of the agricultural area under the same cropping regime and soil type.
The amount of nitrogen available for crop uptake from organic manure may be calculated by sampling and analysis in accordance with Part 2 of Schedule 2.
The total amount of nitrogen in organic manure applied to a holding, whether directly by an animal or by spreading, must not exceed 100 kg multiplied by the area of the holding in hectares.
Slurry or liquid from the treatment of sewage sludge by anaerobic digestion must be incorporated into the ground as soon as practicable and within 24 hours at the latest after application.
The maximum amount of slurry that may be spread at any one time is 30 cubic metres per hectare.
An exemption applies where a storage facility was not used before 1st March 1991 for the relevant purpose but was constructed before that date for such use.
In order to comply with the duty under paragraph (1), the Secretary of State must establish a monitoring programme to assess the effectiveness of the restrictions.
Silage bales must be stored at least 10 metres from any inland freshwaters or coastal waters that effluent escaping from the bales could enter.
For beetroot, Brussels sprouts, cabbage, calabrese, cauliflower, and leeks (individually or in combination), the permitted amount of nitrogen that may be spread is 370 kg/ha.
The occupier must record, within one week of spreading manufactured phosphate fertiliser, the amount of phosphate spread.
The occupier of a holding must not store organic manure (other than slurry), or bedding contaminated with organic manure, except in a covered building (including a greenhouse).
An occupier who sends livestock manure off a holding must, within one week of doing so, record the type and amount of livestock manure.

If the occupier is found in breach of the derogation conditions after the application has been granted but before the calendar year to which the application relates, the Agency may revoke the derogation by sending written notice to the applicant before the calendar year for which the derogation was granted, taking into account the seriousness of the breach.
Each valve on the drainage pipe must be capable of shutting off the flow of slurry through the pipe and must be kept shut and locked when not in use.
The total nitrogen limit for the whole holding imposed by paragraph (1) does not apply where the occupier has been granted a derogation.

Where no nitrogen value is established for an organic manure for the purposes of a provision referred to in paragraph (1), the occupier may not spread that manure in reliance on that provision on a crop referred to in regulation 12 or 13.
The occupier must record the temporary field sites used for free-standing heaps as referred to in regulation 23, and the dates of use.
On an organic holding, nitrogen must not be spread after 31st October.
The occupier must make a record demonstrating that the conditions referred to in regulation 8(6) are met.
No part of a silo, its effluent tank, channels, or pipes may be situated within 10 metres of any inland freshwaters or coastal waters into which silage effluent could enter if it were to escape.
The amount of nitrogen available for crop uptake from organic manure may be calculated by sampling and analysis in accordance with Part 2 of Schedule 2.
The occupier must calculate the amount of phosphorus in the soil that is likely to be available for uptake by the crop during the growing season.
The quantity of livestock manure brought on to or sent off the holding may be calculated by using the standard figures in Part 1 of Schedule 2.

Where any part of an effluent tank is below ground level, the tank must be designed and constructed so that it is likely to continue to satisfy the structural integrity and impermeability requirements of paragraphs 4 and 5 for at least 20 years without maintenance.
Regulation 30 does not apply to a crop growing in a greenhouse.
Regulation 31 does not apply to nitrogen fertiliser spread in a greenhouse.
Organic manure must not be incorporated into ground that slopes in such a way that there may be a run-off to water.

Each sample must be poured into a larger container, stirred thoroughly, and a two-litre sample taken from that container and poured into a smaller, clean container; the two-litre sample must then be sent for analysis.
The slurry or other manure must, if it is reasonably practicable to do so, be thoroughly mixed before the samples are taken; and each sample must be taken from a different location.
When determining restrictions on spreading nitrogen fertiliser, the soil type must be taken into account.
A person must record the month in which slurry, manure, or agricultural effluent is to be spread.
Regulation 20 (closed periods for organic manure) does not apply to the spreading of nitrogen fertiliser in a greenhouse.

Where slurry flows into a channel before discharging into a reception pit and the flow out of the channel is controlled by a sluice, the reception pit must have adequate capacity to hold the maximum quantity of slurry that can be released by opening the sluice.
Storage of organic manure is prohibited within 50 metres of a spring, well or borehole, or within 10 metres of surface water or a land drain (other than a sealed impermeable pipe).
Records of spreading nitrogen fertiliser must include the type of organic manure.
Any tap or valve permanently fixed to a fuel storage tank through which fuel oil can be discharged to the open must be shut and locked in that position when not in use.

The occupier of a new holding with livestock must calculate and record— the amount of storage capacity (in slurry vessels and hardstanding) required to enable compliance with regulation 25, taking into account the amount of manure intended to be spread on land that has a low run-off risk, and
Records of spreading nitrogen fertiliser must include the area spread.
When carrying out the review of the action programme, the Secretary of State must make adequate arrangements to enable the public to prepare and participate effectively.

The bund and the base of the area must be designed and constructed so that they are of sufficient strength and structural integrity that, with proper maintenance, they are likely to remain impermeable to water and oil for at least 20 years.

The base of a silo must be constructed using appropriate hot-rolled asphalt in accordance with BS 5502:Part 21: 1990 (the British Standards Institution code of practice for selection and use of construction materials).
A record of livestock manure brought on to or sent off the holding must include the name and address of the recipient.

A regulatory review must include an assessment of whether the objectives of the regulations remain appropriate and, in so far as they do, the extent to which those objectives could be achieved in a less burdensome way.
Before spreading organic manure, the occupier of a holding must record the area on which the manure is to be spread.
For the purposes of paragraph (6)(c), the panel may request the appellant or the Agency to provide additional information.
The occupier of a holding who spreads organic manure must, within one week of doing so, record the date, the method, and the type of organic manure spread.
Slurry spreading equipment must have a trajectory of 4 metres or more from the ground and be able to achieve a maximum slurry application rate of 1 mm per hour when operating continuously.
The base and walls of any effluent tank, channels, and reception pit must be impermeable.
For grassland on all other soils (not sandy or shallow), the closed period for spreading organic manure runs from 15th October to the following 31st January.
Organic manure storage is prohibited on land having a slope of 12 degrees or more which is within 30 metres of surface water.

An area is designated as a nitrate vulnerable zone for the purposes of these Regulations if it is an area of land that drains into polluted waters, contributes to the pollution of those waters, and is marked as such a zone on a relevant map.
For the purposes of regulation 8, the total amount of nitrogen in organic manure must be calculated by reference to the methods described in regulation 14.
The Agency must, by 31 December 2016, publish the proposals to revise or add to the designation on the Agency's website.
Parts 3 to 8 of UKSI 2015/668 apply only in relation to holdings that are in nitrate vulnerable zones designated for the purposes of these Regulations.
Regulation 9 applies to any silo, slurry or fuel oil storage system whose construction is to be begun on or after 15th June 2013.

The Agency must make recommendations to the Secretary of State as to which areas of land should be, or should continue to be, designated as nitrate vulnerable zones, by reference to the matters in regulation 4(5)(a) to (c), before 10th August 2016 and before 10th August of every fourth year thereafter.

No later than the end of each four-year period, the Secretary of State must identify water that is affected by pollution, or could be if the controls in these Regulations are not applied in the area concerned, using the criteria in Annex I to Council Directive 91/676/EEC.

Where a sampling station has recorded nitrate concentration below 25mg/l in all previous samples taken under the review obligation and no new factor likely to increase nitrate content has appeared, the review cycle is extended so that the first review date is 2021 (instead of 2017) and subsequent reviews occur every eight years (instead of every four years).

A person may spread manufactured nitrogen fertiliser during the closed period on a crop specified in the first column of the table in paragraph (5), provided the rate of nitrogen specified in the second column of that table is not exceeded.
The occupier must record, within one week of spreading organic manure, the amount of phosphate that was supplied for uptake by the crop.

The occupier of a relevant holding must, when separating slurry on the holding into its solid and liquid fractions, do so either mechanically or on an impermeable surface where the liquid drains into a suitable receptacle.
